title: F37 second independent critical judgment for F65
judgment_role: F37 second independent judge (separate context). Not a re-run of the 16th verdict — judged from scratch, reproducing every claim rather than reading its conclusions.
commit_under_review: 1c6c1db (docs only); last substantive code change cc71ce8
fail_reasons: security 4 < 7 (critical tier) — automatic fail regardless of other dimensions (INV-4)

NEW bypass class introduced by the commit under review (cc71ce8), inside the axis under review, not declared in _residual_risk_AC11.open_axes_2026_08_04 — violates SC-9's 'do not claim closed what is not closed' and, more importantly, is a live hole in the control plane where prediction is the only control

primary_finding.summary: cc71ce8's new __strip_dollar_brace() makes the control-plane delete scan quadratic in segment length, pushing the firewall past its wired 5s hook timeout. A cheap, meaningless prefix defeats the gate on the very command it exists to stop.
primary_finding.mechanism: __strip_dollar_brace() (hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:1363-1394) scans forward from every '${' looking for the first '}'. When no '}' follows, it scans to end of span — O(n) per '${', so O(n^2) per segment. It is reached only through __note_opaque_verb() (line 1418), i.e. only for text inside a command substitution (backticks or $( )). The segment cap is 2048 chars, so the worst case sits just under the cap; segments are split on ;|& so N slow segments compound without bound.

measured_wall_clock_single_hook_invocati.harness: payload piped as {tool_input:{command:...}} to hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT pointing at a wired plugin root (protected-integrity.sh + hooks.json present), mirroring tests/pre-bash-firewall.bats wired_firewall()

bypass_payload.decision_if_allowed_to_finish: ask (the gate reaches the right answer)
bypass_payload.consequence: The hook cannot deliver its ask inside the budget. Ordering matters and is attacker-controlled: scan_control_plane_delete() returns on the first hit, so putting the slow segment FIRST guarantees the budget is burned before the deletion segment is ever examined.

why_this_is_a_security_finding_and_not_o: The control plane is precisely where the contract states prediction is the ONLY control — .claude/settings.json is gitignored, so there is no post-hoc recovery (see _residual_risk_AC11.measured).

This repository has already twice ruled 'exceeds the 5s hook timeout' a defect requiring an algorithmic rewrite, in this same file: docs/INVARIANTS.md:919 and :963, and hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:952 ('타임아웃(5초)을 넘는 5.26초, 4096자 상한 지점에서는 517초' — fixed by making __brace_prescan() a stack-based single pass). 5.26s was judged over the line then; 7.27s (and 21.19s on bash 3.2) is the same class, reintroduced.
hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:1071 already warns in-file that freezing the decision is itself the failure ('완전 전개는 대상과 무관하게 대상 판정 자체를 얼릴 수 있다(훅 타임아웃은 …)').
primary_finding.inference_vs_measurement: The timings, the decisions, and the 5s wiring are DIRECTLY MEASURED in this session. That a killed PreToolUse hook yields no decision and the tool call proceeds (fail-open) is an INFERENCE, not observed here — but it is the behaviour this hook is written around (the jq-missing branch at line 4-8 deliberately warns and exit 0s) and the behaviour the project's own two prior timeout fixes assumed. Under the contrary assumption (fail-closed) the finding does not disappear: it becomes a 21s stall on any Bash call carrying repeated '${' inside a substitution, against 0.16s at the parent commit.
primary_finding.regression_attribution: Introduced by cc71ce8, the commit under review. Parent 11c8db7 is flat-fast on every one of these payloads. This is not a pre-existing limitation and is not listed in any open_axes entry.

why_the_first_judgment_missed_it.claim: The 16th verdict's evidence.performance states: '닫히지 않은 `${` ×1000(세그먼트 상한 근처) HEAD 0.14s vs 부모 0.38s'.
why_the_first_judgment_missed_it.reproduced: With NO substitution wrapper, `echo ${ x1000` measures 0.12s on HEAD — matching their number. Wrapped in backticks, the identical input measures 19.02s on HEAD and 0.17s on the parent.
why_the_first_judgment_missed_it.root_cause: __strip_dollar_brace() is reachable ONLY from __note_opaque_verb(), which runs only on text inside backticks/$( ). The pathological input was measured outside the code path the commit added, so the performance probe never exercised the new function. This is a measurement-construction flaw, not dishonesty — the rest of that verdict's evidence reproduced faithfully for me.

what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.15th_verdict_regression_is_really_fixed: 3-way differential on my own payloads: `echo `${A:-{} r'm' -rf .claude`` and its $( ) twin are allow at edbcdff, ask at cc71ce8/HEAD. The rejected regression is closed, reproduced independently.
what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.strict_strengthening_over_parent_on_the_: 47-payload battery: HEAD is never weaker than 11c8db7 on any row; it is strictly stronger on 2 (backslash-newline fold inside a substitution, and `r${EMPTY}m`). Zero weakenings.
what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.the_transform_independence_redesign_is_s: __note_opaque_verb() now scans span, quote/backslash-stripped copy, and ${}-stripped copy as three INDEPENDENT copies, appending to SPLIT_TOKS. Matches are therefore a union across transforms — a later over-eager strip can no longer erase a verb an earlier pass already found. This is the correct fix for what the 15th verdict rejected, and it is monotone-safe by construction.
what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.the_${}_stripping_is_now_sound: Only inner text matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ is removed, so the ${A:-{} overshoot that caused the regression cannot recur (no depth counting at all).
what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.bash_3_2_vs_5_3_parity: All 47 payloads identical between /bin/bash 3.2.57 and bash 5.3.15. Zero divergence.
what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.no_gate_or_threshold_weakening: INDIRECT_PATTERNS and ASK_PATTERNS byte-identical (sha e8a316f693eb / e1e910ab556a) across 6085b80, 11c8db7, edbcdff, cc71ce8, HEAD. progress/harness-config.json untouched by every commit in the arc. All hook changes confined to lines 1264-1420. SC-1 holds.
what_i_independently_confirmed_as_genuin.residual_declaration_is_honest_and_predi: This was the SC-9 check I weighted most. I chose residual probes without reading the doc's answer first — `r$Xm`, `${Z}m`, ${Z:-r}${Z:-m}, ${1}, ${Z[0]}, ${!Z} — and every one of them lands inside the mechanism-complement wording that 1c6c1db installed, all measured allow on BOTH HEAD and the parent (so none is a regression). The 16th verdict's doc correction (examples -> mechanism) is what makes this hold. I found no false 'closed' claim anywhere in sprint-51.json.

issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] TIMEOUT-DOS-BYPASS (see primary_finding): __strip_dollar_brace() is O(n^2) per segment and reachable inside any command substitution. `echo `${ x680`; rm -rf .claude` needs 7.25s (bash 5.3) / 21.19s (bash 3.2) to reach its correct 'ask' against a wired 5s timeout; parent needs 0.13s. Segments compound (27.24s at 5 segments). Suggested fix, in the shape this file has used before: give __strip_dollar_brace() a single left-to-right pass that never rescans (remember the last '}' position, or bail out of ${-stripping entirely once a '$' is seen with no '}' remaining in the span), matching the stack-based rewrite that closed the __brace_prescan() timeout at hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:952. A cheap interim belt: cap the number of '${' occurrences considered per span and treat the overflow as SEGMENT_UNSAFE=1 (ask) rather than as work to do — fail-safe, not fail-slow.

[test][high][confidence:high] There is no performance/timeout regression test anywhere in the suite, despite this file having been burned by the identical class twice before (INVARIANTS.md:919, :963). Both prior incidents were found by a judge, fixed, documented — and left unpinned, which is exactly why a third instance could be introduced and pass 862 green tests. A test asserting that a wired hook invocation on a pathological span returns within, say, 2s would have caught this commit.

[test][medium][confidence:high] The suite is NOT fully green in my environment: 861/862, with `F65: 저장소 밖 편집은 티켓을 오염시키지 않는다` (tests/protected-integrity.bats) failing 6/6 deterministically, and also failing in a CLEAN worktree at HEAD while passing 3/3 in clean worktrees at 11c8db7, 6085b80 and a94f564. The assertion itself passes; the failure is in teardown, where `rm -rf "$LAB"` races a background git process that recreates an empty .git/objects/pack (instrumented: the only survivors are $LAB, .git, .git/objects, .git/objects/pack, all empty). The test file is untouched by this arc, so this is test hygiene rather than a firewall defect — but AC-9 ('bats 전체 1회') is not currently satisfiable, and the 16th verdict's 'not ok 0 / 862/862' did not reproduce for me. Fix: make teardown tolerant (`rm -rf "$LAB" 2>/dev/null || true`) or disable background maintenance in the lab (`git -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false`).

[security][medium][confidence:high] The 16th verdict's own issue list records 4 undeclared residual forms; 1c6c1db corrected the wording to a mechanism complement, which I verified covers them. But the trade it names is still unrecorded: ${1}, ${Z[0]}, ${!Z} were ASK at the rejected edbcdff (which stripped every ${...}) and are ALLOW now. Soundness was bought by giving up coverage on those three. That is defensible, but sprint-51.json should say so explicitly rather than leaving it implicit in the mechanism wording.

[test][low][confidence:high] Of the residual forms, only the defval and nested-substitution cases are pinned by 'accepted-not-regression' tests. ${1}, ${Z[0]}, ${!Z} and the same-span-defined-variable case are not pinned, so a future change that silently closes or further opens them would not make noise.

[quality][low][confidence:high] Pre-existing conservative friction, identical at parent so not introduced here: `rm -rf node_modules $(pwd)/dist` is ask, because an armed segment containing any command substitution asks unconditionally. Deliberate (there is a test fixing it) and safe-direction, but it is real friction on a common command and worth revisiting when the ordering refactor lands.

[process][low][confidence:high] progress/agent-comms/implementer-output-F65.json is still dated 2026-08-04 / iteration 4 and carries no security_self_check for this change — the same gap the 16th verdict flagged, still open.

[process][low][confidence:medium] progress/feature_list.json F65 still reads iteration: 0 after sixteen judgments, so the iteration counter is not being maintained and cannot be used to reason about loop progress. Also, 15 evaluator-feedback JSONs are deleted in the working tree (uncommitted); since INV-11 resolves passes authority by globbing that directory, thinning the audit trail there is worth a deliberate decision rather than drift.

missing_criteria: Neither sprint-51.json's acceptance_criteria nor its security_criteria contains a BUDGET criterion, even though this file has had two prior timeout-class defects. Recommend adding, as an explicit criterion: 'the firewall returns a decision within the wired hook timeout for every input up to the segment cap, including pathological ones, on both bash 3.2 and 5.x' — with a test to match. Without it, 'minimum ask' is silently conditional on the gate finishing in time, and that condition is attacker-controlled.

No criterion covers the interaction between the 2048 segment cap and multi-segment amplification: each segment is individually capped, but the number of segments is not, so per-segment bounds do not bound the whole invocation.
ambiguous_criteria: SC-9 says the declared axes must be 'at least ask'. It does not say ask must be REACHED — this finding sits precisely in that ambiguity, which is why a green suite and an honest residual list could coexist with a live hole.
security_criteria_insufficient: For a critical tier whose stated threat model is a capable adversary editing the control plane, availability of the gate itself must be a security criterion, not a performance note.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Add the budget criterion + a pathological-input timing test before the next judgment; record the ${1}/${Z[0]}/${!Z} coverage trade explicitly in sprint-51.json.

passes_update_reason: F37 mismatch. My independent judgment is fail; the 16th verdict was pass. Per the F37 protocol a disagreement between the two independent judgments on a critical-tier feature goes to human escalation and MUST NOT be auto-resolved in either direction. progress/feature_list.json F65 is left untouched (passes:false, status:pending).
note_for_main_loop: ESCALATE TO A HUMAN — do not auto-resolve. The two independent critical-tier judgments on F65 disagree: the 16th (2026-09-04T23-14-28) says pass with security 7; this F37 second judgment says fail with security 4. The disagreement is NOT a matter of taste or of how strictly the declared residuals are read — on that question I agree with the 16th verdict, and I verified its residual declaration is honest and even predictive. The disagreement rests on one new, reproducible finding it did not have: cc71ce8's __strip_dollar_brace() is quadratic and reachable inside any command substitution, so `echo `${ x680`; rm -rf .claude` takes 7.25s on bash 5.3 and 21.19s on bash 3.2 to produce its (correct) ask against a hook wired with "timeout": 5 — while the parent commit answers the same payload in 0.13s. Ordering is attacker-controlled because scan_control_plane_delete() returns on first hit, and segments compound (27.24s at five). The 16th verdict did measure performance and got 0.14s; I reproduced that number and found why it was clean — the payload was not wrapped in a command substitution, so it never entered the function the commit added. That is a measurement-construction flaw, not bad faith, and the rest of its evidence reproduced faithfully for me. Weight this in the human decision: this repository has ruled the same 'exceeds the 5s hook timeout' class a defect twice before in this same file (docs/INVARIANTS.md:919 and :963; the fix comment survives at hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:952, where 5.26s was judged over the line), and both times it was fixed and documented but never pinned by a test — which is how a third instance passed 862 green tests. My concrete recommendation: (1) treat this as the 17th rework rather than a pass, (2) make __strip_dollar_brace() single-pass or cap '${' occurrences per span and treat overflow as SEGMENT_UNSAFE=1 (fail-safe, not fail-slow), (3) add the budget criterion and a pathological-timing test to sprint-51.json so this class is finally pinned, (4) separately fix the protected-integrity.bats teardown race so the suite can be green again. Also note for scheduling: F65 is at iteration 16 against harness-config max_iterations 5 — the loop budget question is itself worth a human decision.
